items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I mean the first jazz film score was Duke Ellington and it was “Anatomy of a Murder” as I recall.

ctx.x: Well you know into the 1970s there was a club called Slugs on the Lower East Side and I think it billed itself as Slugs and the Far East. And it was out of the way and it was a dive. The music was beautiful but it was physically a dive. Somehow in the late 1970s jazz started to undergo a renaissance in the appreciation of the public. And clubs opened and sometimes clubs closed but many clubs have survived and they are elegant and they have good food and it’s no longer a music that you listen to in a grungy club.…
